title: Payment Flow (Purchase Bill to Vendor Payment)
context: Finance › Payment Flow (Purchase Bill to Vendor Payment)

cards.title: Document reference tracking across the accounts payable hierarchy
cards.body:
The payment flow establishes relational foreign key links across invoice, planning, and voucher tables in Finance.
fDocumentReceipt captures supplier invoice numbers, referenced by fPurchaseBill via ReceiptDocNo foreign keys.
fPurchaseBill detail lines reference IGRNDetailId to bind billed rows to specific warehouse receipts in Inventory.
Payment planning tables Finance.FPaymentPlanDetail reference PurchaseBillId to aggregate outstanding liabilities.
fPaymentVoucher records store PlanId and BillId to establish end-to-end payment auditability across transactions.
Line records maintain RefDocType, RefDocNo, and AccountId to preserve audit trails from bill to voucher.
Foreign key cascades verify that referenced purchase bills exist in active authorized states prior to voucher generation.
This relational architecture ensures complete traceability from physical delivery receipt to financial disbursement.

cards.title: Status cascading and open balance consumption across payment stages
cards.body:
Authorizing a Payment Voucher triggers transactional status cascades that decrement open bill liabilities.
Procedures update BilledQty on IGRNDetail records to prevent duplicate billing against warehouse receipts.
Authorizing fPurchaseBill decrements open advance balances in Finance.FAdvanceAdjustDetail linked to prepayments.
fPaymentVoucher execution updates PaidAmount and DueAmount on linked Finance.FPurchaseBill header records.
Bills with zero remaining due balance transition DocumentStatus to Paid or Completed automatically in the database.
If a voucher is cancelled or reversed, cascade routines restore DueAmount balances on linked purchase bills.
Balance recalculations execute within atomic database transactions to maintain consistency between vouchers and bills.
This synchronization prevents accidental double-disbursements and premature invoice closure.

cards.title: General Ledger posting architecture and GST clearing accounts
cards.body:
Purchase Bill authorization invokes Finance.PBPBFinancePosting to generate General Ledger journal vouchers.
The posting routine debits inventory clearing or expense accounts and credits VendorPayableAccount in FJournalDetail.
Input tax credit lines write to CGST, SGST, or IGST input tax ledgers based on supplier registration.
Payment voucher authorization debits VendorPayableAccount and credits BankAccount in Finance.FJournalDetail.
All posting entries enforce balancing invariants between debits and credits within serialized transaction blocks.
TDC tax engine procedures compute tax distributions and write audit keys back to FPurchaseBillMain.
Stored procedures verify that target accounting periods are open for the division before committing journal rows.
This posting framework ensures accounts payable sub-ledgers reconcile perfectly with General Ledger balance sheets.

cards.title: Payment authorization tiers, approval history, and record immutability
cards.body:
Payment documents transition through Initial, Release, and Authorized lifecycle states during processing.
Authorization thresholds configured in masterdata.mAuthorizationGroup restrict approval permissions by user role.
Approvals write sequential records to Finance.FPaymentApprovalHistory with user session timestamps and comments.
Authorized status triggers database triggers that make header and detail rows immutable against direct updates.
Unauthorized users cannot transition records to Authorized status without completing preceding approval tiers.
Amendments require credit or debit notes rather than direct modification of posted accounting vouchers.
Audit triggers record prior row states to historical archive tables before status transitions execute.
This security architecture protects corporate banking transactions from retroactive administrative tampering.

cards.title: Bank ledger interface, cheque generation, and reconciliation tables
cards.body:
Payment vouchers update bank sub-ledgers and write to Finance.FBankReconciliationDetail upon authorization.
Cheque or electronic transfer details populate fields ChequeNo, ChequeDate, and UTRNo for audit tracking.
Bank reconciliation routines query unpresented cheques to calculate adjusted book balances against statements.
Cancelling a payment voucher invokes reversal procedures that restore open liabilities on referenced bills.
Reversal routines generate offsetting credit entries in FJournalDetail to maintain audit compliance.
Audit logging records all voucher modifications, reversals, and user approval actions with IP timestamps.
Scheduled jobs interface with banking gateways to transmit electronic payment instructions securely.
This reconciliation interface maintains exact alignment between internal ledger cash books and bank accounts.
